s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative skin lesion with erythema and nodules
salient_findings: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque over the right side of the anterior chest wall
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
key_facts: History of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
Underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy
Noticed skin lesion after radiotherapy
Lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
Presentation to dermatology 1 year after initial cancer diagnosis
Erythematous plaque measured 15 × 12 cm
Multiple palpable small nodules within the erythema
Immunohistochemistry negative for ER, PR, and HER2
Skin biopsy showed multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and presentation of erythematous plaque with multiple nodules

shortlist.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation of erythematous plaque with multiple nodules and history of breast cancer

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and radiation therapy, with presentation of erythematous plaque

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels on skin biopsy, along with a history of breast cancer and the appearance of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, supports the diagnosis of cutaneous metastasis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: Inflammatory breast cancer typically presents at the time of initial diagnosis, not a year later, and is characterized by diffuse erythema and edema of the breast, rather than a well-demarcated plaque with nodules.

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
rejected.why: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis involves the lymphatic vessels in the lung, not the skin, and presents with respiratory symptoms, not skin lesions.

rejected.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
rejected.why: Carcinoma en cuirasse is a type of cutaneous metastasis, but it typically presents as a more diffuse, leather-like thickening of the skin, rather than a well-demarcated plaque with nodules.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma is a primary skin malignancy that can present with erythema and nodules, but the presence of carcinoma cells in lymphatic vessels on biopsy suggests a metastatic origin, rather than a primary skin tumor.
